siman_491/ateret-zekenim/part-001.txt.1:_: And one does not bless on spices on Yom Tov that falls on Motzei Shabbat; and so Tosafot wrote in the chapter Hamvi'i, and likewise Mordechai there in the name of Rabbenu Gershom and Rabbenu Meshulam.

siman_491/mechaber/part-001.txt.2:main: When Yom Tov falls on Motzei Shabbat, one says "You have chosen us" and "and You made known to us":

siman_492/chok-yaakov/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) And likewise after Sukkot. Unlike after Shavuot; and in Temim De'im he wrote that men of action and chasidim fast even after Shavuot.
siman_492/chok-yaakov/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) Immediately. And they bless Birkat HaLevana, and one who wishes to fast on Birkat HaLevana — and one who answers amen need not accept again. And see Levush and below siman 566 and 568: on Shabbat when they bless the month, or when it is Rosh Chodesh, they do not bless Birkat HaLevana until the following Shabbat — so too Levush and the customs; and when there is a circumcision or wedding they bless at minchah — so Magen Avraham; and this wedding refers to after Sukkot, for after Pesach they do not make a wedding as stated below siman 493; and if there is a circumcision on a fast day, see above siman 566 and 568 — see there.

siman_492/mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ג: (ג) Immediately on Birkat HaLevana — meaning to exclude what they wrote in the name of Mahariw that they should wait to fast until 17 Cheshvan, which is not so; and they bless in the synagogue on the first Shabbat after Rosh Chodesh for one who will fast on Birkat HaLevana, and after that Shabbat they begin fasting on Birkat HaLevana, and one must accept the fast in the minchah before it; however one who answered amen on one who blessed and intends to fast need not accept again in the minchah before the fast day; nevertheless if afterward he reconsidered not to fast, he is not obligated to fast because of answering amen, since he did not accept the fast explicitly with his mouth. And when there is a circumcision or wedding on that Shabbat when they bless Birkat HaLevana, they are accustomed to bless him at minchah because of the goodness etc.
